checks.reason: The host has one ScrollView(.vertical, showsIndicators:false). The exact authored component contains stacks and fixed rows/controls with no nested or off-axis scroll.

One ObserverBridge.make call site occupies one content entry in the host body. The exact authored bridge imports AlertToast and calls its public NativeQualificationProbe. This is one structural entry per body evaluation; SwiftUI may reevaluate the factory and no once-per-lifetime execution claim is made.

The sentinel Text follows the whole bridge result within the same VStack/scrolling flow. After it the host closes the content stack and applies layout/background measurement; no content branch follows the sentinel.
The scroll closes before the sibling VStack containing Apply next fixture, callback receipt and runtime metadata.
showsIndicators:false is a deterministic host construction parameter before native collection.

The generic host consumes offeredWidth from config with default390, then fixes the scroll to that width and height600. This conformance is restricted to the approved390x600 input/environment identity; it does not admit other caller widths or prove actual screen fit.
Host content receives horizontal16 and top24 padding after the complete component/sentinel stack.

The host installs dynamicTypeSize, layoutDirection and preferredColorScheme from the exact approved configuration; large/light/ltr are the declared fallback values. Runtime child environment values are separately exported.

The host hierarchy uses a vertical stack, background canvas and clear GeometryReaders; there is no overlay/sticky content insertion or async/network/timer-generated UI. onAppear/onChange only update geometry metadata. Fixture index/events change at explicit native controls/callbacks. The admitted component has fixed18 rows and no async content.

Host GeometryReaders export actual global-point viewport/content geometry. Tests retain one public AX snapshot ancestry, its raw frames, the original app screenshot attachment, app-frame rectangle and PNG pixel dimensions. The mapping is explicitly declared; actual origin/alignment/scale/crop validity is a runtime requirement.

The record explicitly declares ieee754-binary64, logical_screen_points, XCUIElementSnapshot/native_CGRect provenance and app-frame-to-original-screenshot mapping. This is source declaration and wiring, not measured runtime map proof.

rect exports original x/y/width/height as Double values directly, including direct width/height rather than endpoint differences. Runtime CGRect fields also enter numerical JSON directly. Foundation JSONSerialization is used without custom decimal formatting, Float32 demotion or geometry rounding. Actual finite binary64 roundtrip behavior remains a runtime proof obligation.

Swift rectangle fields are typed Double. Nonfinite NSNumber values become null with a diagnostic instead of fabricated finite geometry. This source review does not claim the unseen receiver rejects every invalid value; that validation remains mandatory and pending.

Every full sweep calls capture with boundaryRequired:true. Only a reached terminal triggers an actual native staticText identifier query; its match_count is recorded and only count==1 exports the actual target.frame and XCUIElement.isHittable value, queried:true, method and snapshot binding. No geometry flag supplies hittability.

The runtime binding/geometry read follows the original screenshot and executed boundary query, is compared to the snapshot binding/content geometry, and is retained as binding_after_capture/capture_consistent. Actual per-sweep viewport/source immutability, root membership and strict finite containment require independent raw-runtime verification.

The exported performance scope names both actual dispatch targets and the full-sweep terminal boundary. Non-boundary captures retain the defaultfalse switch and do not invent a queried boundary receipt.

initial_finding.resolution: Added actual unique native terminal-hittability provider to full-sweep captures, bound before the post-query runtime check; updated query-scope metadata. ObserverApp.swift unchanged.
